adelaide-university.about:
Adelaide University began teaching in 2026, combining the research strength of the Group of Eight University of Adelaide with the industry-focused University of South Australia. It is organised into colleges covering health and medicine, engineering, business, education and social sciences, creative industries and science (including the renowned wine and agricultural sciences at Waite and Roseworthy).

International students apply directly, through SATAC or (from some countries) through an agent, and must meet the degree's academic and English requirements, from IELTS 6.0 up to 7.0 or more. Medicine and dentistry additionally need the UCAT ANZ or ISAT and an interview.
adelaide-university.aid_intl: Merit-based international scholarships (partial tuition reductions); no need-based aid for internationals.
adelaide-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; entry is by secondary qualification. English requirements are degree-specific, from IELTS Academic 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 60 / PTE 60 at the lowest level, rising to IELTS 6.5 (TOEFL 79, PTE 64) or 7.0 (TOEFL 94, PTE 72) for many degrees. Only tests taken at official centres are accepted. Medicine and dentistry require the UCAT ANZ (or ISAT for international applicants).
top_programs: Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery
adelaide-university.gpa_note: Degree-specific minimum results for your qualification; health and medicine are the most competitive.
requirements: English test meeting the degree's level (IELTS 6.0–7.0+ / TOEFL iBT 60–94 / PTE 60–72)
UCAT ANZ/ISAT and interview for medicine and dentistry
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

australian-national-university-anu.about:
ANU was founded by the Australian Parliament in 1946 as the country's national university and remains one of its most research-intensive institutions, with a compact campus in central Canberra. It is known for the Crawford School of Public Policy, the Coral Bell School of Asia Pacific Affairs, the Research School of Astronomy and Astrophysics and strong programs in computing, economics and law; flexible double degrees are common.

International applicants apply directly through the ANU portal (A$150 fee) and are assessed against indicative entry scores for their secondary qualification, plus ANU's English standard (IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 80). Everyone is automatically considered for the Chancellor's International Scholarship, and residential colleges house most first-year students.
australian-national-university-anu.aid_intl: Merit scholarships: the ANU Chancellor's International Scholarship (partial tuition reduction, applicants assessed for the highest award they qualify for) and other faculty awards. No need-based aid for internationals.
australian-national-university-anu.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; you need an accepted secondary qualification meeting the indicative entry score for your program. English (ANU policy): IELTS Academic 6.5 overall, TOEFL iBT 80 (TOEFL iBT Australia only for tests from 21 Jan 2026), PTE Academic 64, Cambridge C1/C2 176. At-home/online test versions are not accepted. Some programs set higher requirements.
top_programs: Bachelor of Politics, Philosophy and Economics
australian-national-university-anu.gpa_note: Assessed against ANU's indicative entry score for your qualification (high IB/A-level results for competitive programs); some programs add selection criteria.
requirements: Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

institute-of-science-tokyo.about:
Institute of Science Tokyo combines Japan's top engineering university (Tokyo Institute of Technology) with a leading medical and dental university. Its Ookayama and Yushima campuses host schools of science, engineering, materials and chemical technology, computing, life science and technology, medicine and dentistry, with a strong research culture and close industry ties.

Most bachelor's teaching is in Japanese, but the Global Scientists and Engineers Program (GSEP) offers an English-taught route into chemistry and chemical engineering-related fields with Japanese-language training. Tuition is ¥635,400 a year, low by global standards, and MEXT and university scholarships are available.
institute-of-science-tokyo.aid_intl: MEXT and JASSO scholarships plus university scholarships for international students; tuition exemption/deferment possible.
institute-of-science-tokyo.tests: GSEP (English-taught) uses a two-stage document screening followed by later selection; strong maths and science and English proficiency are required. Japanese-taught programmes for privately financed international students require the EJU and Japanese ability. Exact score thresholds are not published.
institute-of-science-tokyo.gpa_note: Very strong mathematics and science preparation is expected.

monash-university.about:
Monash is a Group of Eight research university with its main campus at Clayton in south-east Melbourne, further Victorian campuses, and international campuses in Malaysia and Indonesia. It is internationally known for pharmacy and pharmaceutical sciences, and offers large programs in medicine, engineering, IT, business, law and education, many as double degrees.

International students apply directly or through an authorised agent and are assessed on their secondary qualification plus English Level A (IELTS 6.5, no band under 6.0) for most courses. Direct-entry medicine additionally requires the UCAT ANZ or ISAT and an interview. Merit scholarships and study grants partly offset high fees.
monash-university.aid_intl: Merit scholarships (e.g. Monash International Merit Scholarship, Monash International Leadership Scholarship) and International Study Grants of up to A$10,000; no need-based aid for internationals.
monash-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement as such; entry is by your secondary qualification against course minimums. English Level A (most courses): IELTS Academic 6.5 with 6.0 in every band, or an equivalent approved test. Medicine (direct entry) also requires the UCAT ANZ (or ISAT for international applicants) and an interview.
monash-university.gpa_note: Course-specific minimum scores for your qualification; Medicine, Pharmacy and Law are the most competitive.
requirements: English test (IELTS 6.5, min 6.0 per band, or equivalent)
Interview and UCAT ANZ/ISAT for medicine only
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

nanjing-university.about:
Nanjing University traces its roots to 1902 and is one of China's leading research universities, with its main Xianlin campus in Nanjing. It is known for physics, astronomy, chemistry, geology, Chinese language and literature, history and computer science, and runs a well-established institute for international students.

International applicants submit school records, HSK results, a CSCA report, two recommendation letters and a personal statement online, then take a written exam and interview. Tuition is low (from RMB 21,000 a year), and Chinese Government and Nanjing Municipal scholarships are available.
nanjing-university.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship, Nanjing Municipal Scholarship and International Chinese Language Teachers Scholarship.
nanjing-university.tests: SAT, ACT, AP, IB, A-level or AST scores may be submitted (valid two years) but are not mandatory. From 2026/27 a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report is required. Most programmes are Chinese-taught and need HSK level 5 with at least 180. English-major applicants need IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL 70. Admission includes a written exam and interview.
nanjing-university.gpa_note: Selection on high school record, HSK level, CSCA results, written exam and interview.
requirements: HSK 5 (180+) for Chinese-taught programmes; IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL 70 for English majors

seoul-national-university.about:
Seoul National University is Korea's top public research university, with its main Gwanak campus in southern Seoul and 16 undergraduate colleges spanning humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, business, medicine, agriculture, music and fine arts. Teaching is mainly in Korean, though English-taught courses are growing, and graduates dominate Korean academia, government and industry.

Foreign nationals (with non-Korean parents) apply through the Global Talent Special Admission for Spring (March) or Fall (September) entry. You submit a personal statement and study plan, school records, recommendation letters and proof of Korean or English proficiency; some majors interview. Tuition is low by international standards, and scholarships are available.
seoul-national-university.aid_intl: Merit and need-based tuition scholarships for international students (e.g. SNU Global Scholarship, Korean Government Scholarship Program/GKS); availability varies by semester.
seoul-national-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement; standardized results (SAT, ACT, AP, IB, A-level, IGCSE) may be submitted as supporting evidence. Language: Korean (TOPIK level 3+) or English (TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS Academic 6.0 or TEPS 269); TOEFL Home Edition and IELTS Online accepted. Most courses are taught in Korean. Art, music and PE applicants have practical exams/interviews.
seoul-national-university.gpa_note: Holistic document review of school performance, study plan and recommendations; admitted students are typically top of their class.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
TOPIK 3+, or TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.0 / TEPS 269
Portfolio/practical exam for art, music and PE only
Passport and nationality documents of applicant and parents
Interview if required by the department

the-university-of-auckland.about:
Founded in 1883, the University of Auckland is New Zealand's leading research university, with its main campus in central Auckland and faculties of arts, business, creative arts and industries, education, engineering, law, medical and health sciences, and science. Its engineering, business and health programmes are especially well regarded, and conjoint degrees let students combine two fields.

International applicants apply online and are assessed on their secondary results and English (IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5 at minimum). Most programmes close on 8 December for February entry. Fees range from about NZ$42,000 to NZ$61,000 a year, with partial merit scholarships available.
the-university-of-auckland.aid_intl: Merit scholarships such as the University of Auckland International Student Excellence Scholarship (partial tuition); no need-based aid for internationals.
the-university-of-auckland.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; entry is by your secondary qualification (IB, A-levels, NCEA, US diploma with SAT/ACT/AP, etc.). English: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall with no band below 5.5 is the general undergraduate minimum (One Skill Retake accepted); each programme page lists its own IELTS level. TOEFL iBT, PTE and others accepted at equivalent levels.
the-university-of-auckland.gpa_note: Programme-specific rank scores for your qualification; Engineering, Health Sciences and Law (Part II) are most competitive.
requirements: English test (IELTS 6.0, no band below 5.5, or programme-specific level)
Proof of funds for the New Zealand student visa

the-university-of-melbourne.about:
Founded in 1853, the University of Melbourne sits on a city-edge campus in Parkville and is a member of Australia's Group of Eight research universities. Its undergraduate offer is deliberately broad: a small set of generalist bachelor's degrees (Arts, Commerce, Science, Biomedicine, Design, Music, Fine Arts and others) with majors chosen as you go, after which many students enter professional graduate degrees such as the Juris Doctor, Doctor of Medicine or engineering master's.

International students apply directly online or via an agent, with admission based on the entry score for their secondary qualification plus English proficiency. Fees are high and set per course, but the University automatically considers international applicants for fee-remission scholarships, and a few larger merit awards are available.
the-university-of-melbourne.aid_intl: Merit scholarships only: the Melbourne International Excellence Scholarship (Undergraduate) gives a fee remission to eligible international students starting a bachelor's from 2027 and needs no separate application; a few higher-value Melbourne International Undergraduate Scholarships also exist.
the-university-of-melbourne.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement as such: you are assessed on your secondary qualification (IB, A-levels, a US diploma with SAT/ACT/AP, etc.) against each course's entry score. English: the University's undergraduate English standard, with IELTS Academic the usual test; some courses set higher bands. Official score tables could not be verified automatically.
the-university-of-melbourne.gpa_note: Entry is by course-specific scores for your qualification (e.g. high IB totals or strong A-level grades); competitive courses like Biomedicine and Commerce need top results.
requirements: English test meeting the University's undergraduate standard
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

the-university-of-osaka.about:
The University of Osaka (formerly Osaka University) is a leading national research university with campuses in Suita, Toyonaka and Minoh. It is known for engineering, medicine, immunology, chemistry and the sciences, and most of its eleven undergraduate schools teach in Japanese.

For students without Japanese, two English-taught bachelor's routes exist: the Human Sciences International Undergraduate Degree Program and the International Undergraduate Program in Science (chemistry-biology). These start in October, assess applicants mainly on documents (school records, standardized test results such as SAT/IB/A-level, English proof), and charge Japan's national-university tuition, which is low by international standards.
the-university-of-osaka.aid_intl: Merit scholarships including Japanese Government (MEXT) scholarships and JASSO/private foundation awards; tuition exemptions possible after enrolment.
the-university-of-osaka.tests: English-taught Human Sciences programme: applicants submit a copy of a standardized academic test result (e.g. SAT, ACT, AP, IB or A-level) plus proof of English; screening is document-based, with interviews for some. Japanese-taught degrees require the EJU (Examination for Japanese University Admission) and Japanese proficiency.
top_programs: Human Sciences International Undergraduate Degree Program
the-university-of-osaka.gpa_note: Comprehensive document screening; strong grades and standardized results are expected.
requirements: Secondary school diploma (or conditional offer for IB/A-level in progress)
Standardized test result (SAT, ACT, AP, IB or A-level)

the-university-of-technology-sydney-uts.about:
UTS is a public university on a compact, architecturally striking campus in Sydney's Ultimo tech precinct. It focuses on practice-based learning in engineering, IT, design, architecture, business, communication, health, law and science, and many degrees include internships or a Diploma in Professional Engineering Practice.

International applicants apply online, directly or via an agent, with their secondary results and an English test (IELTS 6.5 with writing 6.0 is the standard level). Applications are assessed on a rolling basis, and the Vice-Chancellor's International Undergraduate Scholarship rewards high achievers.
the-university-of-technology-sydney-uts.aid_intl: Merit scholarships such as the UTS Vice-Chancellor's International Undergraduate Scholarship (partial tuition); US students can use US federal loans.
the-university-of-technology-sydney-uts.tests: SAT is one accepted basis for US-curriculum applicants (at a competitive standard, no published minimum); otherwise entry is by your secondary qualification. English (standard): IELTS Academic 6.5 with writing 6.0; TOEFL iBT 79 with writing 21 (or 4/4.5 on the new 1–6 scale); PTE 58 with writing 50; Cambridge C1/C2 176. Some courses (e.g. nursing, education) require more.
the-university-of-technology-sydney-uts.gpa_note: Course-specific selection ranks converted from your qualification; engineering and IT are competitive.
requirements: English test (IELTS 6.5, writing 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 79, writing 21)
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

the-university-of-western-australia.about:
Founded in 1911, UWA is a Group of Eight university on a riverside campus in Perth. Its bachelor's degrees (Arts, Science, Commerce, Philosophy (Honours), Advanced Computer Science, Biomedical Science and others) feed into professional master's programmes, and it is internationally known for earth and marine sciences, agriculture, and mining and petroleum engineering.

International students apply directly (A$150 fee) or through an agent and are assessed against UWA's entry standards for their qualification plus English competence (IELTS 6.5, no band below 6.0, or Duolingo 125). High achievers are considered for the Global Excellence Scholarship.
the-university-of-western-australia.aid_intl: Merit scholarships including the Global Excellence Scholarship (fee reduction for high-achieving international students) and the UWA International Student Award.
the-university-of-western-australia.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; entry is by your secondary qualification against UWA entry standards. English (minimum standard): IELTS Academic 6.5 with no band below 6.0; Duolingo 125 (Speaking 115, Writing 125, Reading 115, Listening 110); Cambridge C1/C2 170 overall. Some courses require a higher standard.
the-university-of-western-australia.gpa_note: Assessed against UWA entry standards for your qualification (e.g. IB or A-level equivalents of the required ATAR).
requirements: English test (IELTS 6.5, no band below 6.0 / Duolingo 125)
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

universiti-malaya-um.about:
Founded in 1905 as a medical college in Singapore, Universiti Malaya is Malaysia's premier research university, with a large green campus in Kuala Lumpur. It offers bachelor's degrees across engineering, medicine and dentistry, business and accountancy, computer science, law, science, arts and education, with many programmes taught in English.

International students apply directly through UM's online portal for either the October (main) or March intake, submitting pre-university results, English test scores and passport details. Fees are modest by global standards and Kuala Lumpur's cost of living is low, though scholarships for international undergraduates are limited.
universiti-malaya-um.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for international undergraduates; most international students are self-funded or sponsored by their governments.
universiti-malaya-um.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement; admission is by your pre-university qualification (A-levels, IB, foundation, etc.). International applicants must show English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent; minimum varies by programme). Official minimum scores could not be confirmed.
universiti-malaya-um.gpa_note: Strong pre-university results are expected; medicine, dentistry, law and pharmacy are most competitive.

university-of-arizona.about:
The University of Arizona leads NASA missions (such as OSIRIS-REx), builds giant telescope mirrors and has one of the top optical-sciences colleges in the US. The Eller College of Management, hydrology and nursing are also well regarded.

International applicants can apply via the Common App or Arizona's own application; English proficiency can be shown through many tests with published minimums.
university-of-arizona.aid_intl: International students are not eligible for federal aid; early applicants receive priority consideration for merit aid.
university-of-arizona.tests: English minimums: TOEFL iBT 79 (pre-Jan 2026) or 4 (new scale), IELTS Academic 6.5, Duolingo 110, Cambridge 180/C1, PTE etc.; SAT EBRW 580 or ACT English 21 also accepted.
requirements: Secondary school transcript (grades from the last 3-4 years)
English test: TOEFL 79 / 4, IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 110
Application fee (see Arizona website); fee waivers available for eligible applicants
Proof of funds / certification of finances for the I-20 or study permit (after admission)
Valid passport (needed for the visa / study permit)

university-of-calgary.about:
UCalgary is one of Canada's top research universities, close to the Rocky Mountains, with the Schulich School of Engineering, the Haskayne School of Business and strong energy, environment and geoscience programmes tied to the city's industry. Its kinesiology faculty is among the best in the world.

Applications are made directly through UCalgary's online application. Admission is based mainly on grades in required high-school subjects for your curriculum.
university-of-calgary.aid_intl: Entrance awards are available to international students; see UCalgary's awards pages.
university-of-calgary.tests: SAT/ACT not required. English proficiency required for applicants whose first language is not English (see UCalgary admission requirements).
requirements: Secondary school transcript (grades from the last 3-4 years)
Secondary school diploma / final exam results (predicted results accepted when applying)
English test: required if English is not your first language (see UCalgary requirements)
Programme prerequisite subjects / supplementary info for some programmes
Proof of funds / certification of finances for the I-20 or study permit (after admission)
Valid passport (needed for the visa / study permit)

university-of-cape-town.about:
The University of Cape Town, founded in 1829, is South Africa's oldest university and a leading research institution in health sciences, commerce, engineering, law and the sciences. Its campus sits on the slopes of Devil's Peak, and the academic year starts in February.

Applications for a given year open on 1 April and close on 31 July of the year before, with no late applications. International applicants should check the eligibility rules for their school qualification, the international fees handbook and the international and refugee scholarship listings.
university-of-cape-town.aid_intl: International and refugee scholarships are listed by UCT; fees for international students are in the official fees handbook.
university-of-cape-town.tests: Admission based on school-leaving results and UCT's eligibility rules for foreign qualifications; application fee R100 (SADC) or R300 (applicants from outside the SADC region).
